texts.preamble: Kamlesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2019 Cr.R. No.1322/2019 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Cr.R. No.1322/2019 (Kamlesh vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh) Indore, Dated:02/04/2019 Shri Ashish Gupta, learned counsel for the appli Shri Ankit Khare, learned Public Prosecutor for respondent/State. Order
texts.facts: Brief facts of the case are that on 26/03/2010, at about 3.15 pm, Yashwant Sharma, the then inspector during the course of inspection went to Kailash Ice-cream Parlour at Jhabua and introduced himself to the shop keeper. He enquired about the shop keeper and carried out inspection of the shop in the presence of independent witnesses. When the license was asked for, the shop keeper Kailash Patidar could not produce the same, thereafter he was given eight days time to produce the same. During inspection, 3 Kgs., of Ice-cream, 200 packets of Ice-candy and 20 Kgs of sugar along with ice-cream machine and thermocol box were found in the shop for making ice-cream. Sample of 900 grams of Ice-cream was taken through Form 7, money was paid for it and receipt was also taken after completing necessary formalities. One part of the sample along with Form 7 was sent to State Food Laboratory, Bhopal and rest of the two samples were sealed and sent to the office of 'Swasth Pradhikari' Jhabua. Vide the analysis report dated 06/05/2010 of State Food Laboratory, Bhopal, the ice-cream sample was found to be adulterated. On the basis of said report, complaint was filed after taking necessary permission. An appeal was filed against the said conviction and sentence, which was dismissed by First Additional Sessions Judge, Jhabua, in Cri. Appeal No.166/2016 vide judgment dated 02/03/2019 . This judgment is under challenge in the present Kamlesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118542992/ 1 revision petition.
texts.arguments: 04. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the impugned order passed by the Courts below are contrary to the law and facts on record. The Courts below has erred by not appreciating the fact that the public analyst report does not specify the quantity of starch found in the sample which was taken, therefore, it does not indicate that the sample was adulterated or injurious to life. The Courts below has also erred by ignoring the fact that the applicant has been denied of his valuable right under Section 13(2) of 'the Act, 1954'. It is further submitted that there are material contradictions and omissions in the statement of complainant and other witness vis -a-vis their Court statement. Prosecution has miserably failed to produce any material to justify the conviction of the applicant, therefore, he prayed for acquittal of the present applicant. 05. On the other hand learned Public Prosecutor opposes the prayer by contending that after due appreciation of the evidence learned Courts below have found the applicant guilty of the offence hence no interference is called for in the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below. 06.

On the other hand learned Public Prosecutor opposes the prayer by contending that after due appreciation of the evidence learned Courts below have found the applicant guilty of the offence hence no interference is called for in the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below. 06.
